subject: Hosted API pricing — vendor approval path & commit tiers
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Attached is the proposal we discussed (high-level pricing plus two commit tier options and sample monthly estimates): 20261120_redwood_proposal.pdf.

Quick summary:
- Option A: 12-month commitment, $120k annual minimum (~$10k/mo). Per-token price at committed volume: $0.0006/token; overage at $0.0008/token.
- Option B: 24-month commitment, $200k annual minimum with deeper discount: $0.00045/token committed, $0.00075/token overage.

We're flexible on the exact minimum and the overage cadence (monthly vs. quarterly invoicing). Could you confirm what paperwork Procurement needs to move forward? I anticipate Acme will want your preferred vendor form and a PO flow. Happy to sign your vendor form or provide our standard SOW/PO language if that helps speed review.

Also flagging that Finance sometimes requires a W-9 and bank details for ACH. I can attach those if helpful.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm vendor form + PO requirements from your team.
2) Decide which commit option looks closest to your forecast.
3) If needed, we can generate an estimated monthly invoice schedule for your AP team.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: 20261120_redwood_proposal.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bowers <tbowers@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Rishi —

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement had a quick look and a few immediate asks before we can escalate to Legal and Finance:

1) We require our preferred vendor form completed for vendor onboarding — sending as attachment (acme_preferred_vendor_form.pdf). Please fill and return.
2) Acme cannot accept an open-ended monthly invoice with variable unit pricing without a clear estimated annual spend or a guaranteed minimum. Our standard play is: PO with an "Estimated Annual Spend" line and a capped not-to-exceed amount, plus a description of how overages will be charged.
3) For variable usage agreements we usually need a monthly forecast cadence and a clause that limits single-month spikes beyond X% of forecast without prior approval.
4) Please include W-9 and bank details for finance.
5) Legal will want to see SLA language and audit log retention (SOC/Security evidence).

If Redwood can accept a PO formatted like: "Estimated annual spend: $120,000 — Not to exceed $150,000; billing based on actual usage at committed rates; overage billed monthly at agreed overage rate," we can generally move forward. If not, we will need a signed fixed-fee statement of work that maps to that PO.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will:
- Fill our vendor form?
- Accept an estimated-annual-spend PO with a not-to-exceed cap?

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can put this on Legal's queue.

Best,
Sam
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Attachments: acme_preferred_vendor_form.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Marissa / Connor —

Looping you in. Procurement at Acme is pushing for their preferred vendor form and wants a PO with an estimated annual spend + not-to-exceed cap. They're uncomfortable with an open variable invoice without a cap.

Questions:
- Can we accept Acme's vendor form (they usually ask for banking details, ACH, tax IDs)?
- For the pricing structure, would it be reasonable to propose a hybrid: commit tiers expressed as a dollar-month minimum (e.g., $10k/mo) with a per-token conversion for overages, and a contractual not-to-exceed cap equal to ~25% above the estimated annual spend?

I'm thinking: offer Option A (12 months, $120k est, NTE $150k) and commit to monthly forecast updates. Will Legal/Finance flag anything obvious here?

Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Rishi —

We can accept Acme's vendor form provided we redact bank routing details and replace with a statement that bank/co details will be shared directly with Finance during onboarding (Finance prefers that). I'll ask Legal to review the vendor form; often we add a Redwood addendum protecting our pricing schedule and limiting information disclosure.

On the pricing structure: I like the hybrid you proposed. Practical language we've used:
- Contract lists a committed dollar-based minimum (e.g., $120,000/year) with a not-to-exceed cap of $150,000.
- Billing: Redwood invoices monthly for actual usage; if usage < committed monthly prorated amount, the customer pays the committed minimum. If usage > committed, overage billed at the agreed per-token overage rate.
- Forecasting/guardrails: Customer provides a monthly 3-month rolling forecast; single-month spikes >50% require advance notice or approval (or subject to review).

Numbers I recommend we offer as a counter:
- 12 month: $120k committed ($0.00060/token committed), NTE $150k; overage $0.00080/token.
- 24 month: $200k committed ($0.00045/token committed), NTE $250k; overage $0.00075/token.

I'll draft a short SOW that maps the dollar commitments to per-token approximations and includes the forecast/guardrail language. I can also prepare a redlined SOW (20261130_redlined_SOW.pdf) to send back to Acme. Connor — can you prepare the standard W-9 and vendor bank detail stub but indicate "finance to receive full banking details post-signature"?

Marissa
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bowers <tbowers@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Team —

Appreciate the quick internal alignment. A couple of follow-ups from Legal/Finance:

1) Legal still wants to see specific SLA language (uptime + incident response), and retention windows for audit logs. Can you point to a standard SLA we can include in the SOW?
2) Finance confirmed they will accept an Estimated Annual Spend PO + NTE cap as long as the SOW explicitly maps the dollar commitment to the billing cadence and defines overage rates.
3) For the vendor form: we need Redwood to complete the form, and we need either an attached W-9 or a note that Redwood will provide tax/bank details to Acme's Finance team after signature.

We can accept the 12-month path if Redwood will sign to the NTE cap and provide the W-9 placeholder. Legal can then circulate redlines.

Proposed next step from Acme: send the redlined SOW and completed vendor form to procurement@acmehealth.com, copy Legal. If Redwood can add a DocuSign link for the SOW, that will speed our internal approval.

Thanks —
Sam

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing proposal and next steps

Sam —

Thanks — we can do that. Attached: redlined SOW (20261130_redlined_SOW.pdf) that maps the committed dollar minimum to the billing cadence and includes SLA bullet points (99.9% uptime target, incident response P1 within 1 hour, audit log retention 90 days with SOC-2 summary). We've also completed Acme's vendor form (vendor_form_filled.pdf) but left bank routing to be exchanged with your Finance team post-signature as requested.

DocuSign link to the SOW: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456

Recap of the agreement we're prepared to sign:
- 12 month term, committed spend $120,000/year (billed monthly as $10,000 committed minimum).
- NTE cap: $150,000 for the 12-month term. Any overage beyond the NTE requires written approval.
- Overage pricing: $0.00080/token billed monthly.
- Forecasting: 3-month rolling forecast; single-month spikes >50% subject to review.
- SLA & security: 99.9% uptime target; P1 response 1 hour; audit log retention 90 days; SOC-2 summary provided.

If that reads correctly to you, please return the completed vendor form and we will initiate DocuSign for the SOW. Connor — please hold the W-9 and full bank details to send to procurement@acmehealth.com after we receive an executed SOW.

Thanks —
Rishi

Attachments: 20261130_redlined_SOW.pdf, vendor_form_filled.pdf
